question: During the reigns of which three kings of Judah did the word of the LORD come unto Micah the Morasthite concerning Samaria and Jerusalem?
opt1: Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah
opt2: Uzziah, Jotham, and Ahaz
opt3: Hezekiah, Manasseh, and Amon
opt4: Josiah, Jehoahaz, and Jehoiakim
correct: Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah
explanation: Micah prophesied during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. Micah 1:1 (KJV) - "The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem."

question: In Micah 1:2, what cosmic summons is proclaimed, and from where is the Lord GOD designated as witness against the people?
opt1: The kings of the nations are called to assemble, and the LORD witnesses from Mount Sinai
opt2: All people and earth are summoned to hear, and the LORD witnesses from His holy temple
opt3: The priests and Levites are called to tremble, and the LORD witnesses from the mercy seat
opt4: The hosts of heaven are summoned to judge, and the LORD witnesses from the valley of Jehoshaphat
correct: All people and earth are summoned to hear, and the LORD witnesses from His holy temple
explanation: The earth is summoned to hear God's witness from His heavenly sanctuary. Micah 1:2 (KJV) - "Hear, all ye people; hearken, O earth, and all that therein is: and let the Lord GOD be witness against you, the LORD from his holy temple."

question: What catastrophic physical imagery portrays the descent of the LORD when He cometh forth out of His place to judge the earth?
opt1: The seas dry up into dusty deserts, and the stars fall from heaven like unripe figs
opt2: The pillars of the earth shake like reeds in water, and the sun turns black as sackcloth
opt3: Mountains melt under Him as wax before the fire, and valleys are cleft as waters poured down a steep place
opt4: The skies roll up like a parchment scroll, and the great rivers turn into boiling pitch
correct: Mountains melt under Him as wax before the fire, and valleys are cleft as waters poured down a steep place
explanation: God's theophany melts the mountains and divides the valleys. Micah 1:3-4 (KJV) - "For, behold, the LORD cometh forth out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth. And the mountains shall be molten under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as the waters that are poured down a steep place."

question: In the rhetorical questions of Micah 1:5, how does the prophet identify the epicenters of transgression for Jacob and the high places of Judah?
opt1: The transgression of Jacob is Bethel, and the high places of Judah are Hebron
opt2: The transgression of Jacob is Dan, and the high places of Judah are Bethlehem
opt3: The transgression of Jacob is Shechem, and the high places of Judah are Lachish
opt4: The transgression of Jacob is Samaria, and the high places of Judah are Jerusalem
correct: The transgression of Jacob is Samaria, and the high places of Judah are Jerusalem
explanation: The capital cities Samaria and Jerusalem embodied the covenant rebellions of the northern and southern kingdoms. Micah 1:5 (KJV) - "For the transgression of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and what are the high places of Judah? are they not Jerusalem?"

question: What specific sentence of physical ruin did the LORD pronounce upon Samaria in Micah 1:6?
opt1: She would be made as an heap of the field, her stones poured into the valley, and her foundations discovered
opt2: Her ivory palaces would be burned with sulfur and her wells filled with salt forever
opt3: Her walls would be submerged beneath an overflowing flood and her name blotted out
opt4: She would be turned into a perpetual swamp inhabited only by bitterns and wild beasts
correct: She would be made as an heap of the field, her stones poured into the valley, and her foundations discovered
explanation: Samaria was reduced to vineyard plantings with stones poured into the valley. Micah 1:6 (KJV) - "Therefore I will make Samaria as an heap of the field, and as plantings of a vineyard: and I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley, and I will discover the foundations thereof."

question: What fate was decreed for Samaria's graven images, and to what origin and end would her hires return?
opt1: Her idols would be carried captive to Nineveh and dedicated to the worship of Nisroch
opt2: Her graven images would be beaten to pieces, her hires burned with fire, returning to the hire of an harlot
opt3: Her silver shrines would be melted to pay tribute to the kings of Egypt and Tyre
opt4: Her golden calves would be ground to powder and cast into the brook of Samaria
correct: Her graven images would be beaten to pieces, her hires burned with fire, returning to the hire of an harlot
explanation: Samaria's idolatrous wealth, gathered as harlot hire, would return to harlot hire. Micah 1:7 (KJV) - "And all the graven images thereof shall be beaten to pieces, and all the hires thereof shall be burned with the fire, and all the idols thereof will I lay desolate: for she gathered it of the hire of an harlot, and they shall return to the hire of an harlot."

question: How does Micah express his intense personal grief over the impending devastation of his people in Micah 1:8?
opt1: He fasts forty days in the wilderness, weeping like an ostrich and howling like wolves
opt2: He puts on sackcloth and iron chains, crying aloud like a crane and chattering as a swallow
opt3: He goes stripped and naked, making a wailing like the dragons and mourning as the owls
opt4: He sits upon the city wall in dust, crying like a pelican and lamenting as a mourning dove
correct: He goes stripped and naked, making a wailing like the dragons and mourning as the owls
explanation: Micah laments stripped and naked, wailing like dragons (jackals) and mourning as owls. Micah 1:8 (KJV) - "Therefore I will wail and howl, I will go stripped and naked: I will make a wailing like the dragons, and mourning as the owls."

question: Why is the prophet's grief described as inconsolable in Micah 1:9 regarding the calamity?
opt1: "Because the disease hath infected all priests and rulers, from Dan even unto Beersheba"
opt2: "Because the king of Assyria hath surrounded Zion with two hundred thousand chariots of iron"
opt3: "Because the temple treasures are carried away and the altar of the LORD is cast down"
opt4: "For her wound is incurable; for it is come unto Judah; he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem"
correct: "For her wound is incurable; for it is come unto Judah; he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem"
explanation: Samaria's fatal contagion had reached the very gate of Jerusalem. Micah 1:9 (KJV) - "For her wound is incurable; for it is come unto Judah; he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem."

question: In the prophetic lament over the towns of Judah, what tragedy befell the inhabitant of Maroth in Micah 1:12?
opt1: The inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good, but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem
opt2: The inhabitant of Maroth fled into the mountains, but a consuming fire devoured their olive orchards
opt3: The inhabitant of Maroth drank bitter waters, and foreign archers took their sons captive
opt4: The inhabitant of Maroth sought peace with Philistia, but their covenant became a snare
correct: The inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good, but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem
explanation: Maroth waited anxiously for good, yet judgment reached Jerusalem's gate. Micah 1:12 (KJV) - "For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good: but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem."

question: What mourning rite is commanded for the towns of Judah concerning their delicate children being led into captivity?
opt1: "Rend your garments and gird your loins with haircloth, weeping for your sons carried into Babylon"
opt2: "Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee"
opt3: "Cover your faces with ashes and sound the trumpet of woe, for your daughters are sold for silver"
opt4: "Walk barefoot in sorrow through the valleys of Judah, for the glory of your youth hath departed"
correct: "Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee"
explanation: Judah is commanded to shave and enlarge baldness like the eagle for children going into exile. Micah 1:16 (KJV) - "Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee."

question: Against what premeditated abuse of power does the prophet pronounce woe in Micah 2:1-2?
opt1: Plotting military mutiny against King Hezekiah and bribing the captains of the guard with gold
opt2: Offering nocturnal sacrifices upon the high places of Baal and burning incense to the stars
opt3: Devising iniquity on their beds and practicing it at daybreak, coveting and violently seizing fields and houses
opt4: Extorting unjust temple taxes from poor pilgrims and withholding the tithe of grain and wine
correct: Devising iniquity on their beds and practicing it at daybreak, coveting and violently seizing fields and houses
explanation: Woe is pronounced against ruthless elites who plot and execute property confiscation by morning light. Micah 2:1-2 (KJV) - "Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand. And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage."

question: What inescapable divine counter-devise does the LORD prepare against this corrupt family in Micah 2:3?
opt1: "Behold, I will send a famine of seven years upon your storehouses, until ye sell your lands for bread"
opt2: "Behold, I will bring an army from the north whose arrows shall shatter your iron chariots and bronze gates"
opt3: "Behold, I will strike your judges with blindness and deliver your daughters into the hands of the Philistines"
opt4: "Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which ye shall not remove your necks; neither shall ye go haughtily: for this time is evil"
correct: "Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which ye shall not remove your necks; neither shall ye go haughtily: for this time is evil"
explanation: God devises an inescapable yoke of evil judgment against the haughty oppressors. Micah 2:3 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which ye shall not remove your necks; neither shall ye go haughtily: for this time is evil."

question: What doleful lamentation will the despoiled land-grabbers take up in the day of their divine disinheritance?
opt1: "We be utterly spoiled: he hath changed the portion of my people: how hath he removed it from me! turning away he hath divided our fields"
opt2: "Our silver is turned to dross and our gold is plundered: who shall restore our royal inheritances in Zion?"
opt3: "The sword hath consumed our sons and foreign kings occupy our vineyards: the crown has fallen from our heads"
opt4: "We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold trouble from the north"
correct: "We be utterly spoiled: he hath changed the portion of my people: how hath he removed it from me! turning away he hath divided our fields"
explanation: The oppressors will mourn their total loss as their stolen fields are divided. Micah 2:4 (KJV) - "In that day shall one take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, and say, We be utterly spoiled: he hath changed the portion of my people: how hath he removed it from me! turning away he hath divided our fields."

question: What permanent spiritual and civic penalty falls upon the covetous oppressor in Micah 2:5?
opt1: His descendants shall be excluded from the priesthood unto the tenth generation
opt2: He shall have none to cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD
opt3: His name shall be erased from the tribal genealogies of Judah and Benjamin
opt4: He shall never enter through the gates of the sanctuary to present a peace offering
correct: He shall have none to cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD
explanation: The oppressor is stripped of land-allotment rights in the assembly of God. Micah 2:5 (KJV) - "Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD."

question: How did the rebellious people attempt to censor God's true prophets, and what rhetorical question does the LORD answer with?
opt1: They cast the prophets into muddy dungeons, prompting God to ask: "Can a man hide from my all-seeing eyes?"
opt2: They demanded signs of thunder, prompting God to ask: "Have I not fed you with manna in the barren desert?"
opt3: They commanded, "Prophesy ye not", prompting God to ask: "Is the spirit of the LORD straitened? are these his doings?"
opt4: They tore the prophetic scrolls in fire, prompting God to ask: "Is not my word like a fire and a hammer?"
correct: They commanded, "Prophesy ye not", prompting God to ask: "Is the spirit of the LORD straitened? are these his doings?"
explanation: The people sought to silence rebuke, ignoring that God's words do good to the upright. Micah 2:6-7 (KJV) - "Prophesy ye not, say they to them that prophesy: they shall not prophesy to them, that they shall not take shame. O thou that art named the house of Jacob, is the spirit of the LORD straitened? are these his doings? do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly?"

question: How does the LORD indict the predatory behavior of His people against unsuspecting travelers in Micah 2:8?
opt1: They set armed ambushes in the mountain passes and forced merchants to surrender their donkeys
opt2: They demanded tribute from foreign ambassadors and imprisoned traveling scholars of Egypt
opt3: They threw peaceful pilgrims into cisterns and sold their garments to Phoenician sea-traders
opt4: They rose up as an enemy, stripping robes from peaceful passers-by who were averse from war
correct: They rose up as an enemy, stripping robes from peaceful passers-by who were averse from war
explanation: Judah's elite acted like highway robbers against peaceable citizens. Micah 2:8 (KJV) - "Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war."

question: What grievous oppression did the wealthy inflict upon vulnerable women and their children in Micah 2:9?
opt1: They cast women out of pleasant houses and took away God's glory from their children forever
opt2: They forced widows to toil in stone quarries and enrolled orphan boys into foreign mercenary regiments
opt3: They denied food rations to nursing mothers and sold their infants into Egyptian bond-service
opt4: They stripped mothers of their bridal dowries and barred their daughters from entering the temple
correct: They cast women out of pleasant houses and took away God's glory from their children forever
explanation: Evicting widows and depriving children of their rightful heritage robbed them of God's blessing. Micah 2:9 (KJV) - "The women of my people have ye cast out from their pleasant houses; from their children have ye taken away my glory for ever."

question: With what startling expulsion decree does the prophet shatter the complacency of the land in Micah 2:10?
opt1: "Flee ye to the mountains; for the sword of the Chaldeans shall consume the pastures of your delight"
opt2: "Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction"
opt3: "Gird yourselves with mourning; for the crown of Zion is fallen, and your vineyards are given to strangers"
opt4: "Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; for the sanctuary is profaned, and your sacrifices shall not be accepted"
correct: "Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction"
explanation: The promised land, defiled by sin, could no longer provide rest and would violently eject its inhabitants. Micah 2:10 (KJV) - "Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction."

question: What kind of deceitful preacher would the corrupt populace enthusiastically accept as their prophet in Micah 2:11?
opt1: A court astrologer who promises continuous military victories and expanding borders
opt2: A smooth-tongued orator who flatters their ancient royal pedigree and temple sanctity
opt3: A man walking in falsehood who prophesies of wine and of strong drink
opt4: A mercenary seer who demands silver in exchange for visions of harvest prosperity
correct: A man walking in falsehood who prophesies of wine and of strong drink
explanation: The debased people welcomed only prophets who accommodated their drunkenness and self-indulgence. Micah 2:11 (KJV) - "If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people."

question: In the magnificent restoration promise of Micah 2:12-13, how does the LORD describe the regathered flock and their divine Leader?
opt1: Assembled like eagles of Hermon with the Deliverer guiding them upon the peaks of Lebanon
opt2: Mobilized like an army of lions with David their prince marching in triumph toward Jerusalem
opt3: Collected like wheat into the storehouse with the righteous Branch planting them in peace forever
opt4: Gathered like sheep of Bozrah with the Breaker going up before them, their King passing before them and the LORD at their head
correct: Gathered like sheep of Bozrah with the Breaker going up before them, their King passing before them and the LORD at their head
explanation: The Messiah is depicted as 'the Breaker' breaking open the pen and leading His gathered flock to freedom. Micah 2:12-13 (KJV) - "I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men. The breaker is come up before them: they have broken up, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the LORD on the head of them."

question: What shocking butchery and cannibalistic metaphor does Micah utilize to expose the predatory violence of Israel's civil magistrates?
opt1: Plucking skin off God's people, eating their flesh, breaking their bones, and chopping them in pieces as for the pot and caldron
opt2: Tearing them like ravenous wolves in winter and casting their severed limbs to wild desert dogs
opt3: Crushing them under heavy chariot wheels of iron and threshing their bodies like grain upon basalt floors
opt4: Draining their lifeblood into golden flagons to celebrate drunken feasts in the high places of Samaria
correct: Plucking skin off God's people, eating their flesh, breaking their bones, and chopping them in pieces as for the pot and caldron
explanation: Rulers who ought to know justice acted like cannibalistic butchers consuming the flock. Micah 3:2-3 (KJV) - "Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; Who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them; and they break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron."

question: What retribution awaits these oppressive leaders when they cry unto the LORD in the day of judgment?
opt1: The LORD will answer them with consuming lightning and scatter their bones across the Kidron valley
opt2: The LORD will not hear them and will hide His face from them because they behaved themselves ill in their doings
opt3: The LORD will deliver them bound into the hands of the king of Babylon to be blinded and mocked
opt4: The LORD will laugh at their calamity and send swarms of venomous vipers into their fortified bedchambers
correct: The LORD will not hear them and will hide His face from them because they behaved themselves ill in their doings
explanation: Because they were deaf to the poor, God will turn His face away from their cries. Micah 3:4 (KJV) - "Then shall they cry unto the LORD, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings."

question: How does Micah characterize the hypocritical, mercenary criteria of false prophets in Micah 3:5?
opt1: They wear rough garments to deceive, yet take silver bribes to pardon murder and adultery
opt2: They fast publicly in the street corners, yet secretly offer libations to the Queen of Heaven
opt3: They bite with their teeth and cry Peace, but prepare war against anyone who putteth not into their mouths
opt4: They flatter wealthy princes with lies of security, while condemning poor orphans to debt slavery
correct: They bite with their teeth and cry Peace, but prepare war against anyone who putteth not into their mouths
explanation: False prophets tailored their message based entirely on personal bribery and food. Micah 3:5 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him."

question: What spiritual darkness and humiliation will overtake the corrupt seers and diviners in Micah 3:6-7?
opt1: Their tongues will cleave to the roof of their mouth, and their divination stones will turn into sulfur
opt2: They will be smitten with perpetual madness, running naked through the tombs of the valley of Hinnom
opt3: Their idols will fall face down in the dirt, and foreign sorcerers will mock their empty incantations
opt4: Night without vision, the sun going down over them, and seers covering their lips in shame because there is no answer of God
correct: Night without vision, the sun going down over them, and seers covering their lips in shame because there is no answer of God
explanation: The false prophets would suffer total spiritual eclipse, ashamed with lips covered for lack of divine revelation. Micah 3:6-7 (KJV) - "Therefore night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine; and the sun shall go down over the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them. Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded: yea, they shall all cover their lips; for there is no answer of God."

question: In bold contrast to the silenced hirelings, how does Micah describe his own divine prophetic empowerment in Micah 3:8?
opt1: "Truly I am full of power by the spirit of the LORD, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin"
opt2: "I stand as an iron pillar and a wall of brass before all the kings of Judah to proclaim the day of vengeance"
opt3: "The word of the LORD was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I could not stay"
opt4: "The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back from my calling"
correct: "Truly I am full of power by the spirit of the LORD, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin"
explanation: Micah was empowered by the Holy Spirit with righteousness and courage to confront national sin. Micah 3:8 (KJV) - "But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the LORD, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin."

question: With what scathing architectural indictment does Micah condemn the civil leadership of Jerusalem in verse 10?
opt1: "They lay the cornerstones of their palaces with extortion and roof them with robbery"
opt2: "They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity"
opt3: "They pave the courts of the temple with deceit and erect towers upon the tears of the fatherless"
opt4: "They fortify the battlements of David with idolatry and cement their walls with blood of the innocent"
correct: "They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity"
explanation: Civic expansion and architectural splendor built through injustice was equated with building with bloodshed. Micah 3:10 (KJV) - "They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity."

question: What pervasive venality corrupted the three governing institutions of Judah according to Micah 3:11?
opt1: Heads take bribes of vineyards, priests drink sacrificial wine, and prophets sell sacred scrolls
opt2: Heads pervert the poor in the gates, priests sacrifice lame beasts, and prophets practice necromancy
opt3: Heads judge for reward, priests teach for hire, and prophets divine for money
opt4: Heads oppress the stranger, priests marry foreign harlots, and prophets consult the stars of Babylon
correct: Heads judge for reward, priests teach for hire, and prophets divine for money
explanation: All three ruling offices—civil leaders, priests, and prophets—operated exclusively for financial profit. Micah 3:11 (KJV) - "The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the LORD, and say, Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us."

question: Despite their shameless commercialization of sacred duties, what presumptuous religious slogan did the leaders profess?
opt1: "The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, are these"
opt2: "The covenant of David standeth sure, and no enemy can scale our holy walls"
opt3: "We have Abraham to our father, and our sacrifices are sweet incense before the Most High"
opt4: "Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us"
correct: "Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us"
explanation: The corrupt leaders relied on false theological presumption, claiming immunity from disaster. Micah 3:11 (KJV) - "The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the LORD, and say, Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us."

question: What monumental sentence of destruction was pronounced upon the holy city for the sake of its corrupt rulers in Micah 3:12?
opt1: "Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest"
opt2: "Therefore shall the sanctuary be burned with brimstone, and the Ark of the Covenant swallowed up by the earth"
opt3: "Therefore shall the walls of Zion be broken down with iron rams, and her gold carried away into the storehouses of Nineveh"
opt4: "Therefore shall the holy mountain become a salt pit, and the altar of burnt offering an habitation for jackals"
correct: "Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest"
explanation: Zion would be completely plowed like an open agricultural field—a prophecy famously cited a century later in Jeremiah 26:18. Micah 3:12 (KJV) - "Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest."

question: What central moral cause does Chapter 3 assign for the total future demolition of Jerusalem and the temple mount?
opt1: The failure of King Hezekiah to pay sufficient annual tribute to the king of Assyria
opt2: The systemic bribery, perversion of equity, and extortion practiced by the princes, judges, priests, and prophets
opt3: The omission of the daily morning and evening lamb offerings by the sons of Aaron
opt4: The refusal of the army captains to march into battle against the confederacy of Syria
correct: The systemic bribery, perversion of equity, and extortion practiced by the princes, judges, priests, and prophets
explanation: Chapter 3 systematically links Jerusalem's plowing directly to leadership injustice, bribery, and violence. Micah 3:9-12 (KJV) - "Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity ... Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field ... "

question: What glorious eschatological exaltation is foretold for the mountain of the LORD's house in the last days?
opt1: It shall be surrounded by twelve gates of pearls, and rivers of living milk shall stream from its foundations
opt2: It shall be crowned with a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night, and kings shall bring gold from Ophir
opt3: It shall be established in the top of the mountains, exalted above the hills, and people shall flow unto it
opt4: It shall be transformed into a great high plain, and an impenetrable wall of jasper shall guard its borders
correct: It shall be established in the top of the mountains, exalted above the hills, and people shall flow unto it
explanation: In the last days, Mount Zion will be the preeminent center of global spiritual pilgrimage. Micah 4:1 (KJV) - "But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it."

question: What eager invitation will many Gentile nations extend to one another regarding Zion in Micah 4:2?
opt1: "Come, and let us build palaces of cedar in the valleys of Judah, and offer our daughters as handmaids to the King of Israel"
opt2: "Arise, let us present the wealth of Egypt and the spices of Sheba before the golden altar of the Holy One"
opt3: "Let us gather our wise men to learn the ancient wisdom of Solomon, that our kingdoms may flourish in peace"
opt4: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem"
correct: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem"
explanation: Nations will stream to Zion to learn God's ways and walk in His torah. Micah 4:2 (KJV) - "And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem."

question: What universal disarmament and transformation of military weapons will accompany the LORD's righteous judgment among nations?
opt1: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks; nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither learn war any more
opt2: They shall cast their shields into molten bronze for temple gates, and hang their quivers in sacred armories
opt3: They shall burn all war chariots with unquenchable fire, and scatter the iron armor of soldiers into the sea
opt4: They shall break their composite bows over the altars of peace, and establish covenants of trade across all borders
correct: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks; nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither learn war any more
explanation: Weapons of war will be converted into tools of peaceful agricultural cultivation. Micah 4:3 (KJV) - "And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more."

question: With what classic agrarian portrait of personal peace and domestic security does Micah describe the Messianic era?
opt1: "Every man shall dwell inside fortified walls with full granaries, and foreign servants shall plow his fields"
opt2: "They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it"
opt3: "Every family shall inherit a portion of milk and honey, and rain shall fall in due season upon their flocks"
opt4: "They shall plant gardens of pomegranates and olives in peace, and the sound of the war trumpet shall never be heard"
correct: "They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it"
explanation: Peace and freedom from fear under one's own vine and fig tree depict Messianic tranquility. Micah 4:4 (KJV) - "But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it."

question: What unwavering confessional resolve does the faithful remnant declare in contrast to surrounding pagan nations in Micah 4:5?
opt1: "Though the heathen rage and imagine vain things, yet will we bow before the footstool of the Ark of God"
opt2: "The idols of the nations shall perish from under heaven, but our horns shall be exalted in the God of Jacob"
opt3: "For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever"
opt4: "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God"
correct: "For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever"
explanation: The covenant community resolves eternal fidelity to Yahweh's name. Micah 4:5 (KJV) - "For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever."

question: Whom will the LORD assemble and transform into a remnant and strong nation in that day, and where will He reign over them forever?
opt1: The mighty warriors of Judah and the princes of David, restoring their kingdom over all Canaan
opt2: The priests of Levi and the seers of Ephraim, establishing their sanctuary in Bethel
opt3: The wealthy merchants and skilled builders of Jerusalem, rebuilding the walls of Solomon
opt4: Her that halteth, her that is driven out, and her that was afflicted, making them a strong nation with the LORD reigning over them in Mount Zion
correct: Her that halteth, her that is driven out, and her that was afflicted, making them a strong nation with the LORD reigning over them in Mount Zion
explanation: God gloriously restores the lame, outcasts, and afflicted to reign over them in Mount Zion. Micah 4:6-7 (KJV) - "In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted; And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever."

question: Unto what designated pastoral stronghold does the promise of the first dominion and kingdom arrive in Micah 4:8?
opt1: The tower of the flock (Migdal Eder), the strong hold of the daughter of Zion
opt2: The fortress of Zion, the palace of the kings of Judah
opt3: The rock of Rimmon, the refuge of the house of Benjamin
opt4: The hill of Samaria, the heritage of the house of Joseph
correct: The tower of the flock (Migdal Eder), the strong hold of the daughter of Zion
explanation: The first dominion returns to 'the tower of the flock' (Migdal Eder), the stronghold of Zion's daughter. Micah 4:8 (KJV) - "And thou, O tower of the flock, the strong hold of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion; the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem."

question: To what specific, distant imperial location must the daughter of Zion go forth in agonizing travail before experiencing divine redemption?
opt1: She must cross the Jordan into the desert of Moab, and dwell in Petra until her enemies are destroyed
opt2: She must go forth out of the city, dwell in the field, and go even to Babylon, where the LORD shall redeem her
opt3: She must flee southward into the land of Goshen in Egypt, where God will preserve her children
opt4: She must wander through the mountains of Media and Assyria, until the king of Persia proclaims her pardon
correct: She must go forth out of the city, dwell in the field, and go even to Babylon, where the LORD shall redeem her
explanation: Over a century before Nebuchadnezzar, Micah explicitly prophesied exile to Babylon followed by redemption. Micah 4:10 (KJV) - "Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the LORD shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies."

question: What malicious desire do the gathered hostile nations express against Zion, and what divine counsel are they completely blind to?
opt1: They say, "Let her gold be carried away", unaware that God has hidden all temple treasures in subterranean caves
opt2: They say, "Let her walls become dust", ignorant that twelve legions of angels defend her gates
opt3: They say, "Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion", ignorant that the LORD has gathered them as sheaves onto the threshing floor
opt4: They say, "Let her children be slaves", blind to the pestilence waiting to devour their camps at midnight
correct: They say, "Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion", ignorant that the LORD has gathered them as sheaves onto the threshing floor
explanation: The hostile nations assemble to gloat over Zion, unaware they are gathered as grain to be threshed. Micah 4:11-12 (KJV) - "Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion. But they know not the thoughts of the LORD, neither understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor."

question: With what invincible threshing metaphors does the LORD empower Zion to crush her gathered adversaries in Micah 4:13?
opt1: Giving her arrows of lightning and a bow of polished bronze to pierce kings from afar
opt2: Transforming her into an overflowing torrent of basalt stones that sweeps away armies like chaff
opt3: Bestowing upon her a two-edged sword of celestial fire to cut down enemy chariots in the valley
opt4: Making her horn iron and her hoofs brass to beat in pieces many people, consecrating their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth
correct: Making her horn iron and her hoofs brass to beat in pieces many people, consecrating their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth
explanation: Zion is given iron horns and brass hoofs to thresh nations and consecrate their gain to God. Micah 4:13 (KJV) - "Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the LORD, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth."

question: In the siege distress preceding the Messianic dawn in Micah 5:1, what humiliating indignity is inflicted upon the judge of Israel?
opt1: "They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek"
opt2: "They shall strip the judge of Israel of his crown and lead him with iron hooks"
opt3: "They shall bind the judge of Israel with fetters of brass and cast him into a pit"
opt4: "They shall pierce the eyes of the judge of Israel before the gates of Lachish"
correct: "They shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek"
explanation: The ruler of Israel suffers the deep insult of being smitten upon the cheek with a rod during the siege. Micah 5:1 (KJV) - "Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops: he hath laid siege against us: they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek."

question: What historic, momentous prophecy reveals the birthplace, human insignificance, and eternal pre-existence of Israel's ultimate Ruler in Micah 5:2?
opt1: "And thou, Jerusalem the holy, though thou be plowed as a field, yet from thy ruins shall spring forth the King of glory to reign"
opt2: "But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting"
opt3: "And thou, Nazareth of Galilee, though thou be despised among the tribes, out of thee shall arise the Branch of David to conquer the nations"
opt4: "And thou, Hebron city of fathers, out of thee shall step forth the Prince of Peace, whose throne shall endure as the sun"
correct: "But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting"
explanation: The Messiah would originate geographically from little Bethlehem Ephratah, while His eternal origin is from everlasting. Micah 5:2 (KJV) - "But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting."

question: According to Micah 5:3, for what period will Israel be given up before the remnant of His brethren returns?
opt1: "Until seventy weeks are accomplished upon the holy city to finish transgression and make an end of sins"
opt2: "Until the fourth generation hath passed away in the land of their affliction across the Euphrates"
opt3: "Until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel"
opt4: "Until the sanctuary is cleansed and the daily sacrifice restored upon the altar of unhewn stones"
correct: "Until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel"
explanation: Israel is yielded up until the travailing one brings forth the promised King. Micah 5:3 (KJV) - "Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel."

question: How will this divine Shepherd-Ruler govern and preserve His flock in Micah 5:4?
opt1: He shall sit upon an ivory throne with an iron scepter, demanding silver tribute from all kings
opt2: He shall build an impenetrable fortress on Mount Zion and dispatch twenty legions of angelic archers
opt3: He shall conquer with the sword of Goliath, subduing the nations under His feet in continuous war
opt4: He shall stand and feed in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God, and be great unto the ends of the earth
correct: He shall stand and feed in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God, and be great unto the ends of the earth
explanation: The Ruler shepherds His flock in divine power and majesty, achieving worldwide renown. Micah 5:4 (KJV) - "And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God; and they shall abide: for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth."

question: In the face of the ultimate invader ('the Assyrian'), who is proclaimed as the personification of peace, and what leadership counter-force is raised?
opt1: "And this man shall be the peace"; raising against the Assyrian seven shepherds, and eight principal men
opt2: "And the High Priest shall be their shield"; raising twelve judges and twenty-four elders
opt3: "And the Branch of David shall be their tower"; raising three mighty warriors and seven prophets
opt4: "And the Lord of hosts shall be their sanctuary"; raising forty captains and a hundred centurions
correct: "And this man shall be the peace"; raising against the Assyrian seven shepherds, and eight principal men
explanation: The Messiah Himself is our peace, counteracting the enemy with abundant shepherds and principal men. Micah 5:5 (KJV) - "And this man shall be the peace, when the Assyrian shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men."

question: What victory over oppressive empires is achieved by these leaders under the Messiah in Micah 5:6?
opt1: They shall submerge Nineveh under an overflowing river and burn the palaces of Babylon with brimstone
opt2: They shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof
opt3: They shall cast the king of Assyria into a fiery furnace and tear down the high walls of Calah
opt4: They shall carry the gods of Assyria in triumphal procession into the gates of Jerusalem
correct: They shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof
explanation: The oppressors' lands (Assyria and Nimrod) are conquered and neutralized at their very borders. Micah 5:6 (KJV) - "And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders."

question: With what refreshing, life-giving metaphor does Micah portray the remnant of Jacob in the midst of many nations?
opt1: As an overflowing spring of sweet water in a barren valley, quenching the thirst of weary pilgrims
opt2: As the golden rays of the morning dawn, chasing away the thick shadows of pagan darkness
opt3: As a dew from the LORD, as showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men
opt4: As fragrant cedar branches upon the mountains, providing shelter and shade to the wandering tribes
correct: As a dew from the LORD, as showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men
explanation: The remnant dispenses divine grace sovereignly, like heavenly dew dependent on God alone. Micah 5:7 (KJV) - "And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the LORD, as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men."

question: With what fierce, invincible metaphor does the prophet conversely describe the remnant of Jacob among the Gentiles?
opt1: As a swift leopard leaping from high rocky crags to scatter herds of horned cattle
opt2: As a majestic royal eagle striking down serpents in the open field with unswerving claws
opt3: As an unbridled war horse trampling iron shields and bronze chariots in the day of battle
opt4: As a lion among the beasts of the forest and a young lion among flocks of sheep, treading down and tearing in pieces with none to deliver
correct: As a lion among the beasts of the forest and a young lion among flocks of sheep, treading down and tearing in pieces with none to deliver
explanation: Beside their dew-like blessing, the remnant possesses formidable, victorious power over hostile adversaries. Micah 5:8-9 (KJV) - "And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver. Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off."

question: What military reliances and defensive fortifications does the LORD decree to dismantle from the midst of His redeemed people in that day?
opt1: Cutting off their horses, destroying their chariots, cutting off cities, and throwing down all strong holds
opt2: Melting their iron swords into plowshares and burning their composite bows and quivers in fire
opt3: Drying up their mountain cisterns and dismantling their stone catapults and battering rams
opt4: Disbanding their elite bodyguards and removing all bronze armor from their royal arsenals
correct: Cutting off their horses, destroying their chariots, cutting off cities, and throwing down all strong holds
explanation: God purges all fleshly trust in military hardware (horses, chariots, fortifications) so that trust rests in Him alone. Micah 5:10-11 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds:"

question: What occult practices and idolatrous paraphernalia does the LORD promise to eradicate completely from their land?
opt1: Executing necromancers, smashing crystal divination cups, and burning the robes of star-gazers
opt2: Cutting off witchcrafts, soothsayers, graven images, standing images, and plucking up groves
opt3: Outlawing false oaths by Baal, grinding silver amulets into dust, and sealing occult caves
opt4: Banning dream-interpreters, melting gold sun-images, and tearing down the altars of Chemosh
correct: Cutting off witchcrafts, soothsayers, graven images, standing images, and plucking up groves
explanation: God thoroughly cleanses His people from sorcery, soothsaying, and all manufactured idols. Micah 5:12-14 (KJV) - "And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers: Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands. And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities."

question: In the majestic covenant lawsuit (rib) of Micah 6:1-2, what enduring witnesses does God summon to hear His controversy with Israel?
opt1: The sun, the moon, and the twelve constellations of the heavens
opt2: The archangels Michael and Gabriel, and the cherubim of the sanctuary
opt3: The mountains, the hills, and the strong foundations of the earth
opt4: The great deep, the stormy winds, and the rolling waves of the sea
correct: The mountains, the hills, and the strong foundations of the earth
explanation: God calls the ancient, immutable mountains to witness His legal pleading with Israel. Micah 6:1-2 (KJV) - "Hear ye now what the LORD saith; Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice. Hear ye, O mountains, the LORD's controversy, and ye strong foundations of the earth: for the LORD hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel."

question: With what tender, sorrowful question does the LORD confront His ungrateful people, and what foundational redemptive leaders does He remind them of?
opt1: "Why have ye forsaken the fountain of living waters?"; reminding them He gave them Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
opt2: "Have I been a wilderness unto Israel, a land of darkness?"; reminding them He sent Joshua, Caleb, and Samuel
opt3: "What iniquity have your fathers found in me?"; reminding them He provided David, Solomon, and Elijah
opt4: "O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee?"; reminding them He brought them out of Egypt and sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
correct: "O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee?"; reminding them He brought them out of Egypt and sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
explanation: God asks how He wearied them, highlighting His redemption from Egypt through Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. Micah 6:3-4 (KJV) - "O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me. For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam."

question: What historic episode involving Moab and the journey from Shittim unto Gilgal does God command His people to remember so they may know His righteousness?
opt1: What Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him
opt2: What Pharaoh king of Egypt plotted, and how the waters divided at the Red Sea
opt3: What Og the king of Bashan boasted, and how his iron bedstead was captured
opt4: What Sihon king of Heshbon refused, and how his fortified cities were overturned
correct: What Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him
explanation: God overturned Balak's plot through Balaam into blessings from Shittim to Gilgal. Micah 6:5 (KJV) - "O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD."

question: What dramatic, escalating sacrifices does the worshipper propose in Micah 6:6-7 to explore what might appease God's wrath?
opt1: Hecatombs of bullocks, seventy talents of Ophir gold, and lifelong Nazirite vows of silence
opt2: Calves of a year old, thousands of rams, ten thousands of rivers of oil, and even his firstborn for the sin of his soul
opt3: Altars of fragrant Lebanon cedar, silver vessels without number, and seven days of weeping in sackcloth
opt4: Ten thousand turtledoves, royal vestments dipped in purple, and dedication of all palace treasures
correct: Calves of a year old, thousands of rams, ten thousands of rivers of oil, and even his firstborn for the sin of his soul
explanation: The worshipper hyperbolically questions if exorbitant rituals or human sacrifice can atone for sin. Micah 6:6-7 (KJV) - "Wherewith shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old? Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"

question: What profound, timeless triad of divine requirements does the prophet declare in the renowned summary of true godliness in Micah 6:8?
opt1: "To fast twice a week, to give tithes of all possessions, and to observe the solemn feasts"
opt2: "To offer pure sacrifices, to recite the Shema at sunrise, and to cleanse the vessel before eating"
opt3: "To do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God"
opt4: "To defend the borders of Judah, to rebuild the ruins of David, and to keep the Sabbath holy"
correct: "To do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God"
explanation: God rejects external ritualism in favor of justice, covenant love (mercy), and humble fellowship with God. Micah 6:8 (KJV) - "He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?"

question: What dishonest commercial practices in the marketplace does the LORD severely denounce in Micah 6:10-11?
opt1: Counterfeit silver shekels, usurious interest rates charged to widows, and unsealed property deeds
opt2: Watered-down milk, adulterated olive oil, and selling moldy barley at inflated wartime prices
opt3: Taking grain pledges from the starving, selling defective plowshares, and bribing tax collectors
opt4: Treasures of wickedness, the abominable scant measure, wicked balances, and the bag of deceitful weights
correct: Treasures of wickedness, the abominable scant measure, wicked balances, and the bag of deceitful weights
explanation: God categorically condemns fraudulent weights, deceitful scales, and short-measuring customers. Micah 6:10-11 (KJV) - "Are there yet the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the scant measure that is abominable? Shall I count them pure with the wicked balances, and with the bag of deceitful weights?"

question: How does Micah describe the character of the wealthy citizens and inhabitants of the city in Micah 6:12?
opt1: "The rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth"
opt2: "The merchants thereof have allied with Tyre, and their hearts are set on purple linens and Egyptian chariots"
opt3: "The nobles thereof have sold the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes in the open market"
opt4: "The elders thereof have taken bribes in the gate, and have driven the fatherless from their ancestral plots"
correct: "The rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth"
explanation: Social oppression and pervasive mendacity characterized the city's wealthy elite. Micah 6:12 (KJV) - "For the rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth."

question: What curse of internal emptiness and military frustration is pronounced upon the wicked in Micah 6:14?
opt1: "Thou shalt drink, but thy thirst shall burn; thou shalt plant vineyards, but locusts shall consume them"
opt2: "Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword"
opt3: "Thou shalt build marble mansions, but strangers shall inhabit them; thou shalt gather gold, but rust shall destroy it"
opt4: "Thou shalt flee when no man pursueth; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase thee into desert caves"
correct: "Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword"
explanation: Oppressors will suffer perpetual dissatisfaction and their rescued treasures will fall to the sword. Micah 6:14 (KJV) - "Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword."

question: What agricultural futility is decreed as divine chastisement upon their harvests in Micah 6:15?
opt1: Planting fig trees that yield only thorns; digging wells that yield only salt water; sowing wheat that produces weeds
opt2: Clearing stones from terraces only for torrents to wash the soil away; pruning vines only for blight to strike
opt3: Sowing but not reaping; treading olives but not anointing with oil; treading sweet wine but not drinking wine
opt4: Harvesting grain into bags with holes; pressing grapes that burst the wineskins; collecting honey devoured by hornets
correct: Sowing but not reaping; treading olives but not anointing with oil; treading sweet wine but not drinking wine
explanation: The covenant curses of Deuteronomy materialize in complete agricultural frustration. Micah 6:15 (KJV) - "Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil; and sweet wine, but shalt not drink wine."

question: Whose notorious apostate statutes and wicked family counsels were kept by the inhabitants of Judah, resulting in desolation and hissing?
opt1: The abominations of Jeroboam the son of Nebat who made Israel to sin
opt2: The cruel decrees of Manasseh who filled Jerusalem with innocent blood
opt3: The pagan treaties of Solomon who built high places for Chemosh and Molech
opt4: The statutes of Omri and all the works of the house of Ahab
correct: The statutes of Omri and all the works of the house of Ahab
explanation: Judah imported the Baal-worshipping, corrupt practices of the northern dynasty of Omri and Ahab. Micah 6:16 (KJV) - "For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; that I should make thee a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof an hissing: therefore ye shall bear the reproach of my people."

question: With what harvest metaphor does Micah begin his lament over the moral desert of his society, and what tragic social reality does he declare?
opt1: He feels like one seeking summer fruits when only gleanings remain, declaring the good man has perished and they hunt every brother with a net
opt2: He feels like a reaper in an empty barley field, proclaiming that the priests have burned the grain in idolatrous incense
opt3: He feels like a solitary olive shaker, declaring that foreign archers have cut down every righteous counselor in Zion
opt4: He feels like a watchman upon a broken tower, announcing that the princes have fled into Egypt leaving only the poor
correct: He feels like one seeking summer fruits when only gleanings remain, declaring the good man has perished and they hunt every brother with a net
explanation: Micah finds society spiritually barren, with godly people extinct and citizens hunting one another with nets. Micah 7:1-2 (KJV) - "Woe is me! for I am as when they have gathered the summer fruits, as the grapegleanings of the vintage: there is no cluster to eat: my soul desired the firstripe fruit. The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they hunt every man his brother with a net."

question: How does Micah describe the coordinated corruption of the prince, the judge, and the great man, and how sharp are the most upright among them?
opt1: They plot treachery at midnight; the best of them is like a venomous adder and colder than mountain snow
opt2: They do evil with both hands earnestly asking for rewards; the best of them is as a brier and sharper than a thorn hedge
opt3: They exchange silver bribes in the temple courts; the best of them is like a jagged flint and sharper than a razor
opt4: They flatter the people with smooth words; the best of them is like a pit of quicksand and darker than pitch
correct: They do evil with both hands earnestly asking for rewards; the best of them is as a brier and sharper than a thorn hedge
explanation: Judicial corruption was greedily executed with both hands; even the best was as prickly as a thorn hedge. Micah 7:3-4 (KJV) - "That they may do evil with both hands earnestly, the prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward; and the great man, he uttereth his mischievous desire: so they wrap it up. The best of them is as a brier: the most upright is sharper than a thorn hedge: the day of thy watchmen and thy visitation cometh; now shall be their perplexity."

question: What total breakdown of interpersonal trust and domestic intimacy is warned against in Micah 7:5-6?
opt1: Lend no silver to a neighbor, avoid public market squares, and lock the outer gates; for robbers roam the streets freely
opt2: Trust not the words of priests, seek no counsel from elders; for the teachers of the law have accepted foreign gold
opt3: Trust not a friend, put no confidence in a guide, guard mouth from wife; for son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, and a man's enemies are of his own house
opt4: Do not travel in caravans, sleep not under open skies; for wild beasts have multiplied across the desolate hills of Judah
correct: Trust not a friend, put no confidence in a guide, guard mouth from wife; for son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, and a man's enemies are of his own house
explanation: Total societal disintegration destroys all familial loyalty (later quoted by Jesus in Matthew 10:35-36). Micah 7:5-6 (KJV) - "Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom. For the son dishonoureth the father, the daughter riseth up against her mother, the daughter in law against her mother in law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house."

question: Amidst total societal collapse, where does the prophet decisively fix his hope in Micah 7:7?
opt1: "I will hide myself in the secret place of the Most High until the storm of indignation be overpast"
opt2: "I will make my supplication unto the angels of heaven, for vain is the help of mortal man in the day of distress"
opt3: "I will abide in the sanctuary of Zion and offer sacrifices of joy upon the golden altar forever"
opt4: "Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me"
correct: "Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me"
explanation: When all human relationships fail, the prophet looks expectantly to the God of his salvation. Micah 7:7 (KJV) - "Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me."

question: What triumphant cry of faith and resilience does the penitent believer shout against the gloating adversary in Micah 7:8?
opt1: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me"
opt2: "Boast not thy strength, O Babylon: for the sword of the Almighty shall shatter thy gates in a single night"
opt3: "Laugh not at my poverty, O daughter of Edom: for my horn shall be exalted above the mountains of Seir"
opt4: "Mock not my tears, O heathen: for he that toucheth Israel toucheth the apple of the LORD's own eye"
correct: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me"
explanation: The believer expresses unwavering confidence in rising again with the LORD as light in darkness. Micah 7:8 (KJV) - "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me."

question: What attitude does the believer exhibit toward divine discipline, and what fate awaits the enemy who mocked, "Where is the LORD thy God?"?
opt1: Rebelling against the chastisement until an angel delivers them, while the enemy is struck with blindness and falls into a pit
opt2: Bearing the LORD's indignation because of sin until He executes judgment, while the mocking enemy is covered with shame and trodden down as street mire
opt3: Fleeing from the presence of God into the desert of Paran, while the enemy's palaces are consumed with sudden wildfire
opt4: Offering continuous burnt sacrifices to hasten pardon, while the enemy's children are carried into perpetual slavery
correct: Bearing the LORD's indignation because of sin until He executes judgment, while the mocking enemy is covered with shame and trodden down as street mire
explanation: The penitent soul patiently bears God's chastisement; the mocking enemy will be trodden down like street mud. Micah 7:9-10 (KJV) - "I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness. Then she that is mine enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the LORD thy God? mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets."

question: In the day of restoration, what architectural and geopolitical gathering is prophesied in Micah 7:11-12?
opt1: The temple shall be expanded to cover Mount Moriah, and priests shall assemble from Greece, Persia, and the isles of Chittim
opt2: The royal palace shall be established with twelve towers of silver, and gold shall flow from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates
opt3: The walls shall be built, the decree far removed, and people shall come from Assyria, fortified cities, river to river, and sea to sea
opt4: The city gates shall remain open day and night, and foreign kings shall carry the children of Zion upon their shoulders
correct: The walls shall be built, the decree far removed, and people shall come from Assyria, fortified cities, river to river, and sea to sea
explanation: Zion's walls are rebuilt, restrictive hostile decrees removed, and exiles return from across the ancient world. Micah 7:11-12 (KJV) - "In the day that thy walls are to be built, in that day shall the decree be far removed. In that day also he shall come even to thee from Assyria, and from the fortified cities, and from the fortress even to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain."

question: With what pastoral prayer does the prophet intercede for God's vulnerable flock dwelling solitarily in the woods?
opt1: "Lead thy sheep beside the still waters of Shiloh, and let them rest in the green valleys of Hebron beneath the shade of oaks"
opt2: "Guide thy little flock through the wilderness of Zin with thy staff, and lead them into the fertile plains of Sharon"
opt3: "Deliver thy lambs from the mouth of the roaring lion, and gather them upon the holy mountain of Zion in peace"
opt4: "Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage, which dwell solitarily in the wood, in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old"
correct: "Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage, which dwell solitarily in the wood, in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old"
explanation: The prophet petitions the Divine Shepherd to feed His flock with His staff in the lush pastures of Bashan and Gilead. Micah 7:14 (KJV) - "Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage, which dwell solitarily in the wood, in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old."

question: How will the heathen nations react when they witness God's miraculous deeds on behalf of His restored people in Micah 7:16-17?
opt1: They shall lay hand on mouth, ears deaf, lick dust like serpents, move out of holes like worms, and fear the LORD our God
opt2: They shall bring their crowns to Jerusalem, fall upon their faces in the outer court, and learn the Hebrew tongue
opt3: They shall cast their silver idols into the sea, tear their royal robes in terror, and flee into mountain caverns
opt4: They shall send ambassadors with camels laden with frankincense, and plead for a covenant of perpetual peace
correct: They shall lay hand on mouth, ears deaf, lick dust like serpents, move out of holes like worms, and fear the LORD our God
explanation: Overwhelmed nations will be dumbfounded, crawling out of their holes like worms in dread of Yahweh. Micah 7:16-17 (KJV) - "The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf. They shall lick the dust like a serpent, they shall move out of their holes like worms of the earth: they shall be afraid of the LORD our God, and shall fear because of thee."

question: With what sublime doxology celebrating God's unmatched pardon, compassion, and covenant faithfulness does the Book of Micah conclude?
opt1: "The LORD reigneth, let the earth rejoice ... righteous and true are thy ways, thou King of saints ... thy mercy endureth for ever"
opt2: "Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity ... he delighteth in mercy ... will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, and the mercy to Abraham"
opt3: "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting ... who only doeth wondrous things in all the earth"
opt4: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts ... who hath redeemed Zion with judgment and her converts with righteousness"
correct: "Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity ... he delighteth in mercy ... will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, and the mercy to Abraham"
explanation: The book climaxes with an allusion to Micah's name ('Who is like Yahweh?'), extolling God casting sins into the ocean depths and fulfilling mercy to Abraham. Micah 7:18-20 (KJV) - "Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy. He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, and the mercy to Abraham, which thou hast sworn unto our fathers from the days of old."
